theo.name: Theo

mara.name: Mara
mara.blurb: SAMPLE regular. Drives the number 12 bus, early shifts.

chapters.title: SAMPLE · Day 1: First Pot
chapters.summary: SAMPLE chapter. Two regulars, one ordinary morning.

bg.alt: A small corner café in the morning. Steam rises from a kettle on the counter.

steps.text: SAMPLE. You flip the sign to OPEN. The kettle ticks as it warms, and the street outside is still blue with early light.
Two regulars usually come by before nine. You set out the mugs.

steps.speaker: theo
steps.text: Morning! Usual, please. I've got a mock exam at ten, so I need all the help I can get.

steps.prompt: Make Theo something warm. There's no rush.
steps.matchText: Theo wraps both hands round the mug. "You remembered the honey."
steps.otherText: Theo takes a sip. "Ooh, something different. Thanks."

steps.speaker: theo
steps.text: Honestly I was up till three. Everyone else seems so sorted.

options.text: "That sounds like a lot. How are you finding it?"

reply.speaker: theo
reply.text: Kind of... heavy? I keep thinking if I stop, I'll fall behind for good.
Asked Theo an open question. He said he feels he can't stop or he'll fall behind.

options.text: "You should just get an early night tonight."

reply.text: Gave Theo advice straight away. He changed the subject.

steps.speaker: theo
steps.text: Thanks for asking, though. Nobody really does.

bg.alt: The café counter, a little later.

steps.text: Mara comes in after the morning rush, later than usual. Something feels a little different today.

steps.prompt: What's different from last week? Tap anything that's changed. Take your time.

before.alt: Mara last week: smiling, in her bright uniform jacket, with a packed lunch box.

after.alt: Mara today: no jacket, tired eyes, and her lunch box is missing.

steps.doneText: You've noticed enough to start a gentle conversation.

hotspots.label: Her face
hotspots.found: She looks like she hasn't slept much.

hotspots.label: Her jacket
hotspots.found: No uniform jacket. Is she not working today?

hotspots.label: Her hands
hotspots.found: No lunch box. She's holding her phone face down instead.

steps.speaker: mara
steps.text: Just a tea, love. Whatever's easiest.

steps.matchText: "Milk, no sugar. You never forget." A small smile.

bg.alt: A corner table by the window.

steps.prompt: Mara sits by the window. What do you say?

reply.speaker: mara
reply.text: Signed off for a week. Couldn't face the early starts any more. Felt like I was driving on autopilot.

reply.speaker: mara
reply.text: Rough few weeks. I'm off work for a bit. Not sleeping.

options.text: Say nothing for now. Let her settle.

reply.text: You wipe the counter. After a minute, Mara glances up.

reply.speaker: mara
reply.text: I'm off work this week, actually. Bit of a wobble.

steps.prompt: She stirs her tea without drinking it.

options.text: "That sounds hard. Do you want to tell me about it?"

reply.speaker: mara
reply.text: It's just... everything's grey. I used to love the route. Now I dread it.

options.text: "Everyone gets like that. You'll be back to normal soon."

steps.text: Mara wasn't eating, and kept her phone face down.

bg.alt: A corner table by the window.

steps.prompt: Before Mara leaves, what feels like the right next step?

options.text: Gently suggest she talks to her GP about the sleep and the low mood.
options.outcome: Mara nods slowly. "I've been putting it off. Maybe I'll ring tomorrow."

reply.text: Suggested Mara speaks to her GP. She said she might ring tomorrow.

options.text: Offer to save her the window seat tomorrow, if she fancies a chat.
options.outcome: "I'd like that." She finishes her tea this time.

options.text: Tell her exactly what she needs to do to feel better.
options.outcome: Mara listens politely, then picks up her bag a little faster than before.

reply.text: Gave Mara a list of fixes. She left quickly.

bg.alt: The café at dusk, chairs up on tables.

steps.text: SAMPLE. You turn the sign round and stack the chairs. Time to write a few lines in the journal.
Noticing small changes gave me a way in. Listening first seemed to help more than fixing.

chapters.title: SAMPLE · Day 2: A Heavier Afternoon
chapters.skipSummary: SAMPLE. Mara came back to the window seat. She shared that she's been feeling low for a while. You listened, and she agreed to book a GP appointment. She left with a little more hope than she arrived with.

bg.alt: The café in the afternoon, rain on the window.

steps.speaker: mara
steps.text: You saved the seat. Thank you.

steps.speaker: mara
steps.text: SAMPLE. Some days it feels like nothing will change.

options.text: "I'm really glad you came in. I'm here to listen."
Sit with her quietly for a moment.

steps.text: If you ever feel like this, you don't have to wait. Samaritans are free on 116 123, any time.
Mara opened up about feeling low. Listening, and knowing where to point her, mattered.
